I've been doing some aquarium automating lately.

I've been doing some tinkering lately, and I now have a decent computer control system for my aquarium. I have a water solenoid valve to allow water from the house plumbing into a bucket, and a dosing pump to add water conditioner to it. Then I have other pumps to move the conditioned water into a new 15 gallon sump for the aquarium, out of the sump into a grey water bucket where I can drain water out to water the plants outside, and if the grey water bucket gets full, another pump that will move water back out to the drain. It can also control 6 outlets individually to control filters, heater, etc, and there's a thermocouple probe to give me water temperature readings. The computer is built with a raspberry pi to handle the network and a JSON RPC interface and an arduino mega for all the digital IO. It can handle temperature regulation, water changes, report out status. Future enhancements include a fish feeder, ph-based co2 control, and optionally maintaining a quarantine tank (the pumps are in place for it, just no actual tank yet). With any luck, I'll also get it integrated with my amazon echo device. (-=

This is great. Good job. I've been looking into arduino automation with some various shields and voltage switches. I can't step into the arduino world yet, since it would consume most of my free time which is precious at the moment. Any way we could get a sketch-up and some codes for the pi and arduino?

At some point in my copious amounts of spare time, I'll post a detailed write up on my website, and I'll post here when that's put together. Usually I'd write the arduino code myself (I went to school for electronics, and I've been a programmer for most of my carrer), but this time I just used the Dino gem from Ruby which treats it like a big IO expansion board, so no Arduino programming is required for this project. I'm using a SainSmart relay board to control the 120V AC outlets and the 12V DC plugs for the pumps and water solenoid, and that's hooked to the arduino since it has lots of IO pins. I also have a bunch of float switches attached to the Arduino through pull-up resistors to let me know when the various containers get full. The software is all written in Ruby using the Dino gem to control the Arduino and the Jimson gem to create the JSON RPC API, and it exposes basic functions like turning things on or off, reading the status of things and whatnot. Now I'm making a set of small scripts that will use that API to perform high level functions such as temperature regulation, auto-top-off, water changes, etc.
